newsitem.title: INDIA: India refers 11 more state firms to divestment body.
newsitem.headline: India refers 11 more state firms to divestment body.

text.p: India's Industry Ministry on Monday referred 11 more state-owned firms to the disinvestment panel for advice on their partial sale, an official statement said.
The ruling United Front coalition set up the Disinvestment Commission last year to advise the government on partial privatisation of state-owned firms.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition government has already referred 40 state-owned firms to the Disinvestment Commission.

The commission in its first report in February suggested a sale of 25 percent of shares in Gas Authority of India Ltd, 74 percent in India Tourism Development Corporation and 100 percent in Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd.
The commission hopes to complete its recommendations on the first set of 40 state-owned firms by October.

The 11 additional state-owned firms refered to the commission are Hindustan Vegetable Oils Corporation Ltd, NEPA Ltd, Electronic Trade and Technology Development Corporation, Hindustan Prefab Ltd, Hotel Corporation of India Ltd, Ranchi Ashok Bihar Hotel Corporation Ltd, Pyrites, Phospates & Chemicals Ltd, Central Electronics Ltd, Engineering Projects (India) Ltd, Utkal Ashok Hotel Corporation Ltd and Rehabilitation Industries Corporation Ltd.
The government aims to raise 48 billion rupees ($1.34 billion) from divestment of shares in state-firms in 1997/98 (April-March) compared to a target of 50 billion rupees in 1996/97.
